title: Canonical point and stalk data of an open partition by field spectra
statement: Let $k$ be a field, let $Y$ be a scheme over $k$ [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-scheme-over-base], and let $(U_i)_{i\in I}$ be pairwise disjoint open subschemes covering $Y$. For every $i$, let $L_i/k$ be a field extension [def-pc-field-extension] and fix a $k$-isomorphism $e_i:U_i\simeq\operatorname{Spec}L_i$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Write $y_i$ for the unique point of $U_i$, viewed in $Y$. Then $i\mapsto y_i$ is a bijection $I\to Y$, every $y_i$ is closed [def-weil-closed-points], and the map $L_i\simeq\Gamma(U_i,\mathcal O_Y)\to\mathcal O_{Y,y_i}$ induced by the germ is an isomorphism of $k$-algebras. Its composite with the canonical residue quotient $\mathcal O_{Y,y_i}\to\kappa(y_i)$ [def-weil-residue-field] is an isomorphism of $k$-algebras as well. In particular the canonical residue quotient itself is an isomorphism. The index set $I$ may be empty or infinite; no finiteness or separability assumption is made on $L_i/k$.

source.place: Tag 02G7 (lemma-unramified-over-field), part (1): extraction of the point and local-ring identifications for the displayed disjoint union of field spectra; these identifications do not use finiteness or separability.

proof.text: By [def-weil-affine-spectrum], each $\operatorname{Spec}L_i$ has exactly one point, so $U_i=\{y_i\}$ as a subset of $Y$ [def-pc-scheme]. The cover gives surjectivity of $i\mapsto y_i$; pairwise disjointness gives injectivity, since $y_i=y_j$ would belong to $U_i\cap U_j$. Thus it is a bijection, also when $I$ and $Y$ are empty.

source.place: Tag 02G7, lemma-unramified-over-field, part (1), disjoint field-spectrum description; elementary topology of that description

proof.text: For each $i$, the complement $Y\setminus\{y_i\}=\bigcup_{j\ne i}U_j$ is open, since the $U_j$ are open and partition $Y$. Hence $\{y_i\}$ is closed, which is exactly closedness of $y_i$ [def-weil-closed-points]. This uses arbitrary unions of opens, not finiteness of $I$.

source.place: Tag 02G7, lemma-unramified-over-field, proof, discrete-space description; elementary complement calculation

proof.text: Fix $i$. The open-subscheme structure identifies $\mathcal O_{U_i}$ with $\mathcal O_Y|_{U_i}$ [def-weil-open-immersion], so $e_i$ identifies $L_i$ with $\mathcal O_Y(U_i)$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Define an inverse to the germ map by $s_{y_i}\mapsto s|_{U_i}$ for any section on an open neighbourhood $V$ of $y_i$. Here $U_i=\{y_i\}\subseteq V$. This is well-defined: two representatives of one germ agree on some open neighbourhood $W$ of $y_i$ [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk], and $U_i\subseteq W$. Restriction back from $U_i$ is the identity, and the germ of $s|_{U_i}$ equals the germ of $s$. Restrictions preserve ring operations. Thus the germ map is a ring isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 0078, section-stalks: representatives and equality of germs; restriction to an open singleton

proof.text: This is a $k$-algebra isomorphism: a scalar $a\in k$ maps to its structure section on $U_i$, then to its germ; this is the stalk scalar map. Since $e_i$ is over $k$, its section identification sends the same scalar to that structure section [def-weil-scheme-over-base; def-weil-locally-ringed-space-morphism; def-pc-field-extension]. The stalk is therefore a field. Its maximal ideal is zero: a nonzero member would be a unit, forcing the ideal to contain $1$. By [def-weil-residue-field], the canonical residue map is quotient by this zero ideal, hence an isomorphism, with inverse $[r]\mapsto r$. Quotient scalar maps are induced by the stalk scalar map, so it and its composite with $L_i\to\mathcal O_{Y,y_i}$ are $k$-algebra isomorphisms. No step used finiteness, algebraicity or separability.

lean.statement: theorem disjoint_field_spectra_point_stalk_data (k : Type u) [Field k] (Y : Scheme.{u}) (f : Y ⟶ Spec (.of k)) (I : Type v) (U : I → Y.Opens) (L : I → Type u) [∀ i, Field (L i)] [∀ i, Algebra k (L i)] (e : ∀ i, (U i).toScheme ≅ Spec (.of (L i))) (hdisjoint : Pairwise (fun i j ↦ Disjoint (U i) (U j))) (hcover : iSup U = ⊤) (hover : ∀ i, (e i).hom ≫ Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k (L i))) = (U i).ι ≫ f) : Function.Bijective (fun i ↦ (fieldSpectrumOpenPoint (e i)).val) ∧ ∀ i, (fieldSpectrumOpenPoint (e i)).val ∈ closedPoints Y ∧ IsIso (fieldSpectrumOpenGerm (e i)) ∧ (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k (L i)) ≫ fieldSpectrumOpenGerm (e i) = (Scheme.ΓSpecIso (.of k)).inv ≫ f.appTop ≫ Y.presheaf.germ ⊤ (fieldSpectrumOpenPoint (e i)).val trivial) ∧ IsIso (fieldSpectrumOpenGerm (e i) ≫ Y.residue (fieldSpectrumOpenPoint (e i)).val) ∧ (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k (L i)) ≫ fieldSpectrumOpenGerm (e i) ≫ Y.residue (fieldSpectrumOpenPoint (e i)).val = (Scheme.ΓSpecIso (.of k)).inv ≫ f.appTop ≫ Y.presheaf.germ ⊤ (fieldSpectrumOpenPoint (e i)).val trivial ≫ Y.residue (fieldSpectrumOpenPoint (e i)).val) ∧ IsIso (Y.residue (fieldSpectrumOpenPoint (e i)).val)
